rows.source: measured, this repository (fixed voices, not cloning)

notes: WER by voice: Lorenzo 0.27%, Chiara 0.66%. Without the 11 lines that contain digits: 0.52% (lines with digits: 0.32%; numbers are read as words since 19 November, before: 0.32%). Previous version (v0.2.0 (voice-four 135k)): 0.54%.

WER measures intelligibility only: every word understood. It says nothing about naturalness, intonation or the slight metallic trace, where the 0.6–2B models are clearly ahead; no paper reports an Italian listening (MOS) score on this set.

Our 95% interval (0.18–0.91%, bootstrap over the 100 lines, 2613 words) overlaps several systems: statistically the same band, not a clear first place. None of the 164 benchmark sentences is in our training texts.

Not an identical task: the other systems clone two Common Voice reference speakers zero-shot, which is harder than speaking in voices the model was trained on. Read the table as intelligibility at a given size, not as a ranking of voice cloning. SIM (similarity to the reference speaker) therefore does not apply to tiny-voca-it.

Other systems are zero-shot cloning models of 0.6–2B+ parameters; their numbers are copied from the papers named in the table. Our normalisation: lower case, punctuation removed (seed-tts-eval style); papers may normalise slightly differently.
Long lines are read sentence by sentence, as in the playground. Speed measured on one CPU thread, including the vocoder.

roadmap.title: Neural vocoder with a harmonic prior
roadmap.text: Replaced the buzzy DSP output; phase from a pitch-driven pulse train, distilled from Vocos.

roadmap.title: Two product voices: IT1 and EF3
roadmap.text: 6 h of EF3 data generated and screened; voice model fine-tuned on both voices (EF3 mel error -33%).

roadmap.title: Less metallic, no tremble
roadmap.text: Retrained vocoder with a per-voice high-band pulse share; 5-frame pitch smoothing. Both preferred in blind tests.

roadmap.title: Public benchmark and vocoder over a range of pulse shares
roadmap.text: MiniMax Italian test set (this page); vocoder fine-tuned so every per-voice setting is in distribution.

roadmap.title: Streaming
roadmap.text: Sentence-level streaming in the browser: playback starts after the first sentence while the rest is synthesised. Next: chunked streaming inside long sentences, and a Python streaming API.

roadmap.title: New voices Lorenzo and Chiara, much stronger emotions
roadmap.text: Two designed voices with 5 h of speech each, 150 emotion-congruent sentences per emotion (5× more), a voice-similarity filter, and a pitch-change loss against tremble. Data generation now ~2.4× faster (CUDA graphs).

roadmap.title: Smaller downloads: lean and quantized ONNX
roadmap.text: Signal-processing tables computed in the graph (47 → 28 MB); the page now loads an int8 version of 8.6 MB with the same intelligibility. fp16 (14.6 MB) and int4 (5.9 MB) variants are also built.

roadmap.title: Numbers read the Italian way
roadmap.text: Cardinals, decimals, percentages, euro amounts, times, dates and ordinals become words before phonemisation, identically in Python and in the browser.

roadmap.title: Releases 0.2.0 and 0.3.0
roadmap.text: Checkpoints, ONNX in four precisions (fp32 28 MB, fp16 15 MB, int8 9 MB, int4 6 MB), model card, samples and checksums on GitHub Releases.

roadmap.title: Clearer highs: texture loss above 2 kHz
roadmap.text: A loss that asks for the recorded amount of high-band detail instead of its average: detail 0.88 → 0.93 (Lorenzo), 0.91 → 0.95 (Chiara); preferred blind on both voices. A 26% larger model gained only ~1% and was not adopted.

roadmap.title: tiny-voca-it-zs: zero-shot voice cloning
roadmap.text: A separate, bigger model (about 8–10M parameters) with its own neural voice-fingerprint network: record 15 seconds and speak in that voice instantly, in the browser, with no training. Trained on hundreds of Italian voices; tiny-voca-it stays the small two-voice model.
